newsitem.title: USA: "Air Force One" takes off at U.S. box office.
newsitem.headline: "Air Force One" takes off at U.S. box office.

text.p: "Air Force One," a hijack thriller starring Harrison Ford as the president of the United States, soared to the top of the box office in its opening weekend, according to studio estimates released Sunday.

The film earned about $37.1 million, and was followed by "George of the Jungle" with $13.2 million and defending box office champ "Men in Black" with $12.6 million. The only other new entry in the top 10 was the children's film "Good Burger," which opened in fifth with $7.3 million.

"Air Force One" smashed several records along the way, as well as earning warm praise from the real president, Bill Clinton, who told reporters over the weekend that he saw it twice and it was a "very good movie."

But he pointed out that the film took some liberties with the facts: the action takes place aboard the president's Boeing 747, and the filmmakers equipped it with an escape pod and a back door, neither of which exist, Clinton said. One other key difference was that Ford earned a reported $20 million, exactly 100 times Clinton's salary.
The film is released by Columbia Pictures, a unit of Sony Corp..

A studio spokesman said "Air Force One" is Ford's biggest opener, breaking the benchmark of $31.5 million set by the "Star Wars" reissue earlier this year. It's also the biggest opening for an "R"-rated movie, beating the $36.3 million launch of "Interview with the Vampire" in November 1994.
Additionally, "Air Force One" is the biggest opening for the second half of the summer (from the July 4 weekend onward), beating the $27.5 million opening of "True Lies" in 1994.

The movie is also on track to be Sony's third consecutive $100 million movie, following "Men in Black," which has earned $194.3 million, and eighth-placed "My Best Friend's Wedding," which passed the $100 million mark on Saturday.
Audiences across the board flocked to see "Air Force One," said Jeff Blake, president of Sony Pictures Releasing, which distributes the film in North America.
"It appeals to both the younger audiences looking for an action movie and to adult audiences looking for a full meal of a movie."
Overseas, the movie will be distributed by Walt Disney Co.'s Buena Vista distribution unit, and Blake was confident it would hold the same sort of appeal.
"This certainly isn't just a film for Americans about the president," he said.
"Air Force One" earned an average of $12,710 from 2,919 screens, more than double the $5,817 average of "Good Burger," which was released by Paramount Pictures, a unit of Viacom Inc..

Disney's "George of the Jungle" held steady at second in its second weekend, and has now earned $48.1 million since its July 16 release. Its drop of 20 percent from last weekend was the smallest in the top 10, while its $5,168 average was third overall.
Columbia's "Men in Black," which had ruled the box office for the past three weekends, dipped 34 percent this weekend, and its average was $3,962.

Fourth place went to "Contact," with $9.5 million, which takes its three-week total to $64.8 million. The Jodie Foster sci-fi picture is released by Warner Bros., a unit of Time Warner Inc.. Falling 41 percent from last weekend, it averaged $4,105 per screen.
